name: file-access-guard-prose
body:
The file-access prose of the distributed agents and the agent-builder template. Four distributed agent prompts — `spec-review.md`, `spec-writer.md`, `plan-writer.md`, `plan-review.md` — carry a `## File access (strict)` section whose "you may read any file" line contradicts the frontmatter read-guard; this component rewrites that section in each to state the rule plainly (graph state is reached only through the apg tools the agent actually holds; never read those node/transient files directly; ordinary source files behind code FQNs stay readable with `read`, all without naming the graph-state filesystem paths). It also extends `agent-builder.md`'s "Permission shape common to every generated agent" list and its step-6 verify checklist so every generated agent carries the same positive rule, not just the permission deny.

This is a markdown-prompt-text change only. The delivered artifact is the embedded constant, not the repo-tree `.md`: the prompt templates are `include_str!` constants in the binary (the AGENTS constant in src/main.rs) written to the user-level suite by `apg.install_suite`. No Rust control flow and no observable CLI behavior changes.

Anchoring (delivery, not behavior): the distributed agent prompts are embedded constants delivered to the user-level suite by `apg.install_suite`, so the durable delivered artifact is the embedded text plus its install path, and the coverage spine anchors to the Rust that embeds and delivers the templates — `apg.main` (the `include_str!` embedding consts) and `apg.install_suite` (the install path that writes them) — never to a `.md` path. That is a delivery-semantics choice, NOT a claim that the templates are unscannable: once the markdown frontend this spec adds lands, `opencode-suite/agents/*.md` become scanned File/Struct nodes, and a scanned `.md` File FQN is a legitimate `implemented-by` target — the code-FQN universe is Module/Struct/Function/File records with no `status` set (src/main.rs:1342-1364), and `classify_code_ref` grades Real/Pending/Drift off that universe independent of file extension (src/layers.rs:1295-1329). No exclusion of the template tree is required. The plan therefore carries a delivery task with `modifies apg.install_suite` as the embedding/delivery anchor; it claims the existing embedding/install path, and no fake behavior change to `apg.main` is claimed. See `solution.note.embedded-template-anchor` / `solution.note.markdown-anchoring` and `requirements.note.file-access-guard-coverage-anchoring`.

The spine also reaches `solution.container.agent-install` (`apg.cmd_init`, `apg.install_suite`) through `domain.entity.agent-prose` / `domain.entity.permission-grant` (the requirement `read-guard-prose` and its children drive those entities). `agent-install` is the pre-existing `apg init` install/delivery path — it embeds and installs the same templates — so the plan claims its anchors on the same delivery-anchor basis. That coverage reach is intentional and explained, not an accidental demand. See `requirements.note.file-access-guard-coverage-anchoring`.
